\subsection{Adjacency Pruning: Correctness and Speedup}
\label{sec:ablation-pruning}

By Lemma~\ref{lem:adjacency-constraint}, if two consecutive facets in an orbit
ordering both have positive dwell time, they must be adjacent in the facet
graph~$G_K$.
Corollary~\ref{cor:adjacency-pruning} therefore allows discarding any
$(S, \sigma)$ for which some consecutive pair $\sigma(k), \sigma(k{+}1)$
(cyclically) is non-adjacent in~$G_K$.
We verify empirically that this pruning discards no optimal orbit, and measure
its speedup on a fixed test dataset.

\paragraph{Variants.}
Table~\ref{tab:ablation-variants} lists the two algorithm variants compared.
V0 is the unpruned reference; V1 is the production algorithm.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{lp{9cm}}
\toprule
Variant & Description \\
\midrule
V0 & Unpruned HK2017: exhaustive search over all subsets~$S$ and all cyclic orderings~$\sigma$ of~$S$ \\
V1 & Pruned HK2017: for each~$S$, restricts to orderings~$\sigma$ that form a Hamiltonian cycle in~$G_K[S]$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:adjacency-pruning}) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Algorithm variants compared. V0 is the most trusted baseline
  (fewest assumptions, simplest code path). V1 is the production algorithm.}
\label{tab:ablation-variants}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Test polytopes.}
Table~\ref{tab:ablation-dataset} describes the 38 test polytopes.
Random polytopes use a fixed seed (42) and height range $h \in [0.5, 2.0]$.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{llrl}
\toprule
Group & $F$ & Count & Description \\
\midrule
Random generic    & 5--8 & 20 & 5 random 4-polytopes per facet count \\
Random Lagrangian & 6--8 & 15 & 5 random products per pair: $\triangle{\times}\triangle$ ($F=6$), $\triangle{\times}\square$ ($F=7$), $\square{\times}\square$ ($F=8$) \\
Regression cases  & 7--8 &  3 & Fixed polytopes known to trigger degenerate KKT systems \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Test polytope dataset. All random polytopes use seed~42, $h \in [0.5, 2.0]$.
  Regression cases: $(3,4)$~at~$\theta{=}0°$ and $(4,4)$~at~$\theta{=}0°$ trigger
  rank-deficient KKT systems; the hypercube exercises the LU fast path.}
\label{tab:ablation-dataset}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Correctness.}
V0 and V1 return identical capacities on all 38 test polytopes (maximum
absolute difference $< 10^{-8}$).
This confirms that adjacency pruning discards no optimal orbit on this dataset,
consistent with Corollary~\ref{cor:adjacency-pruning}.

The three regression cases additionally verify correct handling of degenerate
KKT systems:
$(3,4)$~at~$\theta{=}0°$ (expected $3\sqrt{2}/2 \approx 2.121$) and
$(4,4)$~at~$\theta{=}0°$ (expected $2.0$) both require a null-space search
when the LU factorization detects rank deficiency;
the hypercube (expected $4.0$) is solved by the LU fast path without SVD.
All three capacities match their expected values to within $10^{-6}$.

\paragraph{Speedup.}
Table~\ref{tab:ablation-speedup} shows mean computation times; standard deviations
are shown in Figure~\ref{fig:ablation-timing}.
Pruning is neutral at small facet counts (adjacency graph is nearly complete
for $F \le 6$) and gives approximately $3\times$ speedup at $F = 8$.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{rrrrrrr}
\toprule
& \multicolumn{3}{c}{Random generic} & \multicolumn{3}{c}{Random Lagrangian} \\
\cmidrule(lr){2-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-7}
$F$ & V0 (ms) & V1 (ms) & Speedup & V0 (ms) & V1 (ms) & Speedup \\
\midrule
5 &   0.5 &   0.5 & $0.9\times$ & --    & --   & --           \\
6 &   3.5 &   2.6 & $1.4\times$ &  3.1  &  3.1 & $1.0\times$  \\
7 &  28.4 &  15.3 & $1.9\times$ & 29.0  & 15.1 & $1.9\times$  \\
8 & 255.8 &  80.5 & $3.2\times$ & 258.2 & 85.9 & $3.0\times$  \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Mean computation time (ms) for V0~(unpruned) and V1~(pruned),
  $n = 5$ samples per group per facet count; standard deviations shown in
  Figure~\ref{fig:ablation-timing}.
  Lagrangian products not available at $F = 5$ (minimum $F = 6$ for
  $\triangle{\times}\triangle$).
  Pruning overhead is negligible at $F \le 6$ (dense adjacency graph);
  speedup grows to ${\sim}3\times$ at $F = 8$ as the adjacency graph becomes sparser.}
\label{tab:ablation-speedup}
\end{table}
